# Bogie

> The Go service next to your Rails app. Bogie is a command-line tool that scaffolds an API-only, Postgres-only Go service with Rails-style generators (new, g scaffold, g model, g controller, g job, g authentication) that also wire the code in. It builds on Gin, sqlc with pgx, goose, River and Kamal. The generated app never imports Bogie. MIT licensed, v0.1.0, Go 1.25 or newer.

Install: `go install github.com/bogie-go/bogie@latest`. Then `bogie new blog && cd blog && bogie db:prepare && bogie server`.

Every generated app follows six rules: ctx first on anything doing I/O; interfaces declared where they are consumed; the domain package imports nothing third-party; constructors return (T, error); *gin.Context never travels below the controllers; no util, helpers or common packages. Each app ships an AGENTS.md with the rules, the commands and a recipe per task.

## Guides

- [Getting started](https://bogie-go.com/docs/getting-started.html): Install Bogie, generate a new service, and get it migrating, seeded and serving.
- [Models and migrations](https://bogie-go.com/docs/models.html): Add a table with g model, change one with g migration, and run it through db:*.
- [Resources, controllers and routing](https://bogie-go.com/docs/controllers.html): Scaffold a whole resource or write a controller by hand, and see how either gets registered.
- [Authentication](https://bogie-go.com/docs/authentication.html): Guard a route group with a middleware: a shared secret, a bearer token, or a machine client's key.
- [Services](https://bogie-go.com/docs/services.html): Give logic that is not CRUD a package of its own, with no HTTP in it.
- [Background jobs](https://bogie-go.com/docs/jobs.html): Add River to an app made with --jobs and write a worker that runs beside it.
- [Configuration and credentials](https://bogie-go.com/docs/configuration.html): The environment variables, the encrypted settings file, and what staging means here.
- [Testing and CI](https://bogie-go.com/docs/testing.html): Where tests live, what bin/ci runs, and what doctor checks before either does.
- [Deploying](https://bogie-go.com/docs/deploying.html): One Docker image, every role, shipped with Kamal 2 to staging and production.
- [Conventions and agents](https://bogie-go.com/docs/conventions.html): The six rules every generated app keeps, and why the layout is Rails-shaped on purpose.
- [From Rails](https://bogie-go.com/docs/from-rails.html): A dictionary: what each Rails thing is called here, where it lives, and what has no equivalent.
- [Command reference](https://bogie-go.com/docs/commands.html): Every bogie command, every generator and every make target, in one place.

## Source and design

- [Repository](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie): the tool, MIT
- [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md): every decision and its reasoning
- [STATUS.md](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md): what works today and what is next
- [FROM_RAILS.md](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie/blob/main/docs/FROM_RAILS.md): the Rails-to-Bogie dictionary

## Not

Not a framework, not full-stack (API-only, no views), Postgres only, not a Rails replacement: it runs beside the Rails app.
